intro.h2: Tile that looks like it belongs on Cape Cod
paragraphs: Cape Cod Tileworks has done custom tile in Harwich, MA for decades. In February 2022 the business marked 27 years in its Harwich building, and it still designs and installs tile projects. Its Facebook page sums it up in three words: design and installation.

The work is easy to spot. Pebble backsplashes with ceramic fish and a mermaid swimming across them. A tile map of Cape Cod set into a white tile wall. Pebble fireplace surrounds, and patios that used to be bare cement slabs. Owner Lane Meehan is a RISD graduate who helps you pick the right tile, and Tom Meehan, a second-generation installer, sets it.

services.h2: Custom tile in Harwich, MA: what Lane and Tom create

items.name: Custom mosaics and tile murals
items.blurb: One-of-a-kind pieces drawn for your house: a Cape Cod map set into a tiled wall, carved owls and flowers among river pebbles, sea life tucked into a backsplash. Lane designs the piece and it is laid out by hand before installation.

image.alt: Tile mural of a cream Cape Cod map on deep blue tile above a white subway tile wall

items.name: Bathroom and shower tile
items.blurb: From quiet marble-look porcelain with a woven border and niche, to 12 by 24 porcelain pulled together for a rich look, to navy herringbone. Builders like Schoolhouse Construction have used Cape Cod Tileworks on many bathroom remodels.

image.alt: Shower in marble-look porcelain tile with a basketweave mosaic border and recessed niche

items.name: Kitchen and bar backsplashes
items.blurb: Backsplashes that tell a story or simply finish a kitchen well. One family bought tile for two new bathrooms here, then came back and had Cape Cod Tileworks install their kitchen backsplash, and called the results fabulous.

image.alt: Pebble mosaic bar backsplash with ceramic fish and a mermaid above a butcher block counter and hammered sink

items.name: Fireplace surrounds
items.blurb: A fireplace is a natural place for something personal. Photos show a surround in cream pebble mosaic with small fish and reeds worked into it, framed by white painted trim, the same coastal style as their backsplashes.

image.alt: Fireplace surround in cream pebble mosaic with small fish and reed details inside white trim

items.name: Tile design and selection
items.blurb: Not every customer needs installation. Homeowners and contractors come to Lane for help choosing tile, then have their own builder install it. One couple says they were guided to the perfect tile for two new bathrooms, and another reviewer says the owner knows her stuff.

image.alt: Pebbles, blue glass and hand-cut tile pieces laid out on paper for a custom mosaic design

about.text: Cape Cod Tileworks is owned by Lane Meehan, a graduate of the Rhode Island School of Design, and ran from its building in Harwich for 27 years. In February 2022 the business posted that it had walked out of that building for the last time, adding that it is still here to help design your next project. Tom Meehan is a second-generation tile installer and a technical writer for JLC and Fine Homebuilding magazine. Together they design tile and install it, from coastal pebble mosaics to clean, simple showers.

image.alt: Relief mosaic of a carved owl and flowers set among white river pebbles

process.h2: How a tile project comes together

steps.title: Call Lane
steps.text: Call (508) 246-6324 and describe the room, the feel you want and any pieces you already love.

steps.title: Design and select
steps.text: Lane draws on her RISD design training to help you choose tile, colors and any custom mosaic or mural elements.

steps.title: Lay out the art
steps.text: Custom mosaic pieces, pebbles and glass are laid out by hand on paper before they go on the wall, as their photos show.

steps.title: Install
steps.text: Tom, a second-generation installer, sets the tile. Or your own contractor installs it, as some customers prefer to do.

service_area.h2: Tile design for Harwich and Cape Cod homes
service_area.text: Cape Cod Tileworks is based in Harwich, Massachusetts, and Google lists it at 705 Main St. Its projects include kitchens and wet bars, bathrooms, fireplaces and outdoor patios, with a coastal style that suits the Cape. If you are elsewhere on the Cape and want to know whether Lane and Tom can take on your project, call (508) 246-6324 and describe what you have in mind.

items.q: Can you design a custom mosaic for my house?
items.a: Yes. Custom work is what Cape Cod Tileworks is known for: pebble backsplashes with ceramic fish and a mermaid, a tile map of Cape Cod, carved owls and flowers among river pebbles. Lane designs each piece, and they have written that they look forward to recreating a look for a new customer.

items.q: Do you install, or only sell tile?
items.a: Both. The Facebook page describes the business as design and installation. Tom Meehan, a second-generation tile installer, sets tile, and one family had their kitchen backsplash installed after buying tile for two bathrooms. Other customers have their own contractor install the tile Lane helps them choose.

items.q: Is the Harwich shop still open?
items.a: In February 2022, after 27 years, the business posted that it had walked out of the building for the last time, and that it is still here to help design your next project. Google still lists 705 Main St, Harwich, so call (508) 246-6324 before visiting.

Yes. Schoolhouse Construction Inc. says it has worked with Cape Cod Tileworks for many years on many kitchen and bathroom remodeling projects. Lane can help your builder pick materials, and the Facebook page shows before and after bathrooms done with Schoolhouse.

Yes. In August 2021 Cape Cod Tileworks shared a project where a plain cement slab became a tiled outdoor living space. They wrote that tile is not just for inside the house. Call to talk about patios, outdoor showers or other outdoor ideas for your home.

final_cta.h2: Have a tile idea for your Cape house?
final_cta.text: Call Lane to talk it through, from a simple shower to a one-of-a-kind mosaic.
